note: Illustrative standard VAT / GST rate matrix by jurisdiction, applied to the group's real intercompany flows (royalty / service / goods legs from supply_chain) to size the indirect-tax cash impact and non-recoverable leakage. Rates are STANDARD national rates and the recoverability flags are typical-case simplifications — they ARE publicly checkable but change over time, so verify the current rate and the registration / recovery position per entity before relying on these figures. This is reference data, not VAT advice. The VATable base it is applied to is real (from supply_chain); the rate matrix and recoverability flags are the illustrative seed.

default.basis: no indirect tax modelled for this jurisdiction

jurisdictions.basis: Germany standard VAT 19% — input VAT recoverable for a taxable person making taxable supplies (reverse-charge on cross-border B2B)
France standard VAT (TVA) 20% — input VAT recoverable for a fully-taxable distributor
United Kingdom standard VAT 20% — input VAT recoverable; post-Brexit import VAT via postponed accounting
Netherlands standard VAT (BTW) 21% — input VAT recoverable for a taxable trading company
Ireland standard VAT 23% — input VAT recoverable for a taxable person; cross-border B2B reverse-charge
Switzerland standard VAT 8.1% (in force 1 Jan 2024) — modelled as a non-recoverable leakage on the IP-principal cost base (illustrative; recovery depends on registration / taxable-supply ratio)
India GST standard slab 18% — input tax credit modelled as blocked / non-recoverable on the toll-manufacturing leg (illustrative; ITC depends on registration and output mix)
United States — no federal VAT; state sales / use tax applies at retail only and is not modelled on these wholesale intercompany legs (effective 0% for this analysis)
